title: Moving Away From Animal Testing

content.v: In June 2024, the Chinese actress Huo Siyan posted a video on Xiaohongshu. She shared how she and her husband discovered an injured
beagle
by the roadside. It turned out that the poor dog had come from a lab. The couple took her home and named her Pearl. Their story has drawn public attention to animals used in lab testing.
Animals have long played an important role in scientific studies. In the 1880s, Louis Pasteur conducted experiments on sheep and
demonstrated
that germs cause some diseases. In the 1970s,
treatments
for a serious skin disease were used on animals before being given to humans. In 1974, Rudolf Jaenisch introduced viral DNA into mice. Genetic study grew quickly after that.
Today, animal testing is required for many products. From
cosmetics
to medicines, new chemicals are often tested on animals first. It is said that more than 115 million animals are used in experiments every year.

Lab testing on animals is not like taking your pet to the vet. Lab animals are harmed in many ways. Some tests even require the animal to die. That’s the sad but true situation for millions of mice, rabbits, dogs, and other animals.
Back in the 17th century, people had different opinions about animal testing. Many people disliked it. They believed that animals should not be harmed for humanity’s sake.
In recent years, more and more people are saying “no” to animal research. Some countries have
banned
the testing of certain products on animals. Scientists have been working to offer non-animal methods. For example, they have created 3D
chips

from human cells. These chips work like tiny human organs. They are used to find out how human systems respond to drugs. Some scientists remove cells from a cancer patient’s tumor. These cells are then used to test different treatments. Researchers also make use of computer models. They can
predict
how a medicine might affect us. These methods help improve the understanding and treatment of the human body. They are also faster and cheaper than animal testing.
Old habits die hard. But non-animal methods will one day replace animal experiments. This will be a good thing not just for animals, but for human health in general.
